title: Impact of Citric Acid Etching on Biocompatibility and Osseous Organisation of a Natural Bovine Bone Mineral: Preliminary Results of an In-Vitro/In-Vivo Study
authors: Rothamel D, Schwarz F, Herten M, Berndsen K, Fienitz T, Ritter L, Dreiseidler T and Zöller J in Magjarevic R, Dössel O and Schlegel WC (Eds.), IFMBE Proceedings 2009; 25(11): 259–262.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss cerabone (sintered bovine bone) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Abstract, verbatim (no separate conclusion section): “The aim of the present study was to evaluate the influence of superficial etching of a xenogenous bone mineral on cell proliferation and bone regeneration. A granular bone substitute material [BSM] (cerabone® [CB], botiss medical, Berlin, Germany) was superficially etched using citric acid (Acid [CBA]). CB and CBA were allocated into 96 non -binding well plates and incubated with 1×104 human osteoblast-like cells (SaOs-2) per well under standardized conditions. After 2 hours, 3 and 7 days a LDH- Assay was used for photometric evaluation of cell proliferation (n=8). LDH values were transferred into cell amounts using a standard curve and analyzed for statistical difference. Additionally, cell morphology was investigated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) (n=3). In the in -vivo part, CB and CBA granules were used for lateral augmentation of the maxillae of four beagle dogs and covere” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
